There is no `pkgver()` function, so version computation is static and safe. The top-level scope contains only safe variable assignments, with no command substitution, `eval`, or remote code execution. The `source` array fetches only the intended release artifact and license file. Running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will safely download and verify these sources without executing any build or prepare steps. No evidence of malicious behavior is present in the global scope or source definitions.
</details>

<security_assessment>

<details>
The .SRCINFO file defines metadata for the `zync-bin` package, including source URLs, checksums, and dependencies. The source is a prebuilt `.deb` package hosted on GitHub at the official `zync-sh/zync` repository, which aligns with the project's stated upstream. The license file is also sourced from the same trusted repository. Both sources have matching, non-skipped `sha256sums`, indicating integrity verification is performed. There are no signs of obfuscated commands, unexpected network requests, or execution of downloaded code in this file.

The package depends on standard system libraries (webkit2gtk, libappindicator, etc.), typical for a GUI application. It provides and conflicts with `zync`, indicating it is a binary replacement for a potential non-binary version. No scripts or build instructions are present in this file, and the sources point directly to official release artifacts. While the source is a binary `.deb`, which limits code-level verification, this is common for `-bin` AUR packages and does not constitute a security issue by itself.

As this is a `.SRCINFO` file, it is auto-generated and used for metadata distribution in AUR. It does not execute any code. The content reflects standard AUR packaging practices, with no evidence of injected malicious logic, data exfiltration, or unauthorized system access. The decision remains SAFE based on the absence of malicious indicators.
</details>

<security_assessment>

<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard Arch Linux package build process for `zync-bin`, a binary version of the zync SSH client. It fetches a prebuilt `.deb` file from the project's official GitHub releases page (https://github.com/zync-sh/zync/releases), which is a common and expected practice for `-bin` packages. The source URL is predictable and matches the declared upstream, and the SHA-256 checksums are provided and not set to 'SKIP', indicating verified integrity.

The package extracts the data archive from the `.deb` file and installs the contents under `${pkgdir}`, which is standard behavior for repackaging Debian packages on Arch. It also installs the LICENSE file from the upstream source. All operations are transparent and confined to expected packaging steps. No obfuscated code, suspicious downloads, or unauthorized system modifications are present.

The dependencies and metadata are consistent with a modern GUI application (WebKit for rendering, libappindicator for tray integration), and no post-install hooks or scripts perform network access or system-wide changes. The package does not modify files outside its scope or collect sensitive data. Everything aligns with safe, conventional AUR packaging practices.
</details>

<details>
This file is not executable code — it is a raw HTML snapshot of the GitHub web page for the LICENSE file of the zync-sh/zync repository (the file's head is GitHub page boilerplate and the tail shows the rendered license content, which is a standard MIT License text: "MIT License / Copyright (c) 2026 zync.sh ..."). No shell scripts, PKGBUILD logic, or install-time commands are present, so nothing in this file executes during package build or install.

All network references (github.githubassets.com, api.github.com, collector.github.com) are normal GitHub page asset/telemetry URLs belonging to the project's own upstream host; they are only referenced as HTML attribute values and are not invoked by any packaging code. There is no obfuscation, no encoded/decoded payloads, no curl-bash style download-and-execute, and no attempt to read or exfiltrate local data.

The only notable issue is a packaging hygiene quirk: the LICENSE file shipped in this AUR package contains the entire GitHub HTML page rather than the plain license text, indicating the file was saved from a browser instead of fetched as raw content. This is sloppy but not malicious, and the embedded license text itself is the standard MIT license.
</details>
